title: Reinforcement of the Inboard Flap Track No. 2 Rib Attachment at the Wing Rear Spar

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Wing Trailing Edge — Flap Support Structure

abstract: Thicker rib and a redistributed bolt pattern at the inboard flap track number two attachment on the wing rear spar, introduced after fretting and elongated holes were found on aircraft in high-cycle short-sector operation.

sections.reason: Elongated attachment holes and fretting product were found at the inboard flap track number two rib during scheduled inspection on aircraft operating more than four sectors a day. Twenty-four findings were recorded across the tracked short-haul population between 2015 and 2018, with the earliest at 21000 flight cycles. The mechanism is fretting under the reversing flap load rather than classical fatigue, and it is aggravated by the relatively low clamp-up achieved by the original single-row bolt pattern. Two aircraft required an oversize repair of the rear spar boom, which is a five-day operation on wing.
sections.description: The flap support rib D5730125554505 is replaced by a thicker item and the fitting D5730121797468 at the rear spar interface is renewed with a redistributed bolt pattern that spreads the introduction load over five fasteners instead of three. The upper cleat GIR438406-76 is added to close the load path into the spar web, and the barrel nuts AGS934342-5A are replaced by a longer-grip variant to restore clamp-up. Faying surfaces receive a solid-film lubricant to remove the fretting mechanism. Drawings D57301146439 issue E and D57300042173 issue F carry the revised rib geometry and the bolt pattern. Access is through the trailing edge panels in zones 525 and 624 with the flap in the fully extended position; the flap does not need to be removed.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 3.4 kg per aircraft. No electrical load change. The rib is not interchangeable with the previous item because the bolt pattern differs, and a mixed installation on one wing is not permitted. The repeat detailed visual inspection of the attachment is retained but its interval is tripled, and the associated mirror inspection from below is deleted. IPC and AMM content for ATA 57-30 and the flap rigging procedure in ATA 27-50 required amendment.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z10057 in November 2019. Two bulletins are available for retrofit: an eddy current inspection of the existing attachment, then the reinforcement itself. Embodiment takes about three days per wing and is normally done at a scheduled base maintenance visit.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation, CG shift below 0.02 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z10057, absorbed in the wing trailing edge assembly station
